_readme: PenAI configuration. Copy this file to config/config.json (the packaging
script does that for you) and edit it. JSON has no comment syntax, so every
field is documented in this _readme array. The launcher ignores _readme.
Any key you leave out keeps the default shown below. A malformed value is
reported as a warning in the log and the default is used instead.
server.port ............ First TCP port tried for the llama.cpp server.
Bound to 127.0.0.1 only, never to a public address.
Ports below 1024 are refused (they need root on
Linux) and the default 8080 is used instead.
server.portScanFrom .... Start of the fallback range used when server.port is
already taken. Must be below server.portScanTo.
server.portScanTo ...... End of the fallback range (inclusive).
model.file ............. Empty string means auto-detect: the launcher uses
models/model.gguf if it exists, otherwise the
largest .gguf file in models/. A bare filename is
resolved inside models/ so the drive stays portable;
an absolute path works but is not portable.
llama.ctxSize .......... Context window in tokens. This is the main memory
knob: for this model the KV cache costs about
144 KiB of RAM per token, so 4096 tokens is about
0.56 GiB on top of the model weights, and 16384
tokens is about 2.25 GiB. The launcher measures the
RAM actually available at startup and halves the
context until the estimate fits, so a large value
here is a ceiling and not a promise.
llama.threads .......... 0 means auto-detect from the logical CPU count.
Set a fixed number only if you want to leave cores
free for other work.
llama.parallel ......... Number of concurrent request slots. Each slot gets
its own share of the context, so raising this on a
single-user drive lowers the usable context.
llama.flashAttn ........ "auto", "on" or "off". Anything else falls back
to "auto", which lets llama.cpp decide per build.
llama.extraArgs ........ Extra llama-server command line arguments, passed
through verbatim as separate array elements, for
example ["--no-warmup"]. No shell is involved.
launcher.openBrowser ......... Open the default browser on startup.
launcher.startupTimeoutSecs .. How long to wait for the server to report
healthy before giving up. Loading a 2.5 GB
model from a slow USB stick can genuinely
take minutes, hence the 300 second default.
launcher.instancePort ........ Loopback port used only as a single-instance
lock, so a second launch focuses the running
instance instead of starting a second server.
launcher.storePort ........... Loopback port for the small chat-storage
sidecar. Must differ from instancePort.
launcher.portableStorage ..... true keeps chats on the drive, in
data/chats/, so they travel with it. false
means chats stay only in the browser's local
storage on that computer and nothing is
written to the drive.
logging.maxFileBytes ... Rotate the log once it passes this size (bytes).
logging.keepFiles ...... How many rotated log files to keep in data/logs/.
ui.temperature ......... Default sampling temperature offered by the web UI.
ui.topP ................ Default nucleus sampling value.
ui.maxTokens ........... Default cap on tokens generated per reply.
ui.systemPrompt ........ Default system prompt sent with each conversation.
_network: OFF BY DEFAULT, and the only part of PenAI that can reach outside this
machine. With enabled=true a globe button appears next to the composer and
you can fetch one page at a time by typing its address. The launcher makes
the request with curl and hands the page text back as an attachment you
What it still will not do: the model cannot fetch anything by itself, there
is no crawler and no search, and any address that resolves to this machine
or this network (127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, .local) is refused so a
drive plugged into an office network cannot be used to probe it.
Treat a fetched page as untrusted text: it is written by someone else and
the model reads it. timeoutSecs is clamped to 5-120, maxKilobytes to
_search: Search is off unless you name a provider, because there is no key-free
search API worth depending on and scraping an engine's HTML breaks every
searxng  - your own SearXNG instance. No key. Set url to its base
address, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8888. A LAN or localhost
address is allowed HERE, because you configured it; result
links are still held to the usual no-private-addresses rule.
brave    - api.search.brave.com. Set apiKey to your subscription token.
tavily   - api.tavily.com. Set apiKey to your API key.
WARNING: an apiKey written here sits in plain text on a removable drive.
Anyone who picks up the pendrive can read it. Use a key you can revoke.
The query itself leaves the machine when you search. Only the query -- the
model cannot search or fetch on its own, and a result is only retrieved
